prose: Surge AI extended its DAYJOB benchmark family to tax: 50 professional assignments across preparation, compliance and advisory work, testing whether agents show professional judgment on underspecified problems. The flagship example: an agent correctly told 'Anna' that two proposed condo sale dates both qualified for the $250,000 home-sale exclusion, but missed that moving out in August 2024 meant she would stop satisfying the two-of-five-years residence rule around August 2027.

Across five attempts, Astra never surfaced that deadline; Opus caught it every time. The point of the benchmark is exactly that gap - a tax adviser should flag consequential issues the client didn't know to ask about. Earlier DAYJOB releases covered healthcare and finance.
highlights: DAYJOB: Tax - 50 professional tax assignments for agent evaluation
Tests judgment on underspecified problems, not just correct answers
Astra missed a consequential filing deadline 5/5 times; Opus caught it 5/5
Follows DAYJOB releases for healthcare and finance
